question: Does changing the fixed coordinate-bit factor base change PDP top-form outcomes when planted points are sampled from matched selectors across the entire 2^27 domain, and can point-derived features predict a lower interval-midpoint proxy for a held-out base?
prior_label_exposure: The seven-base common-support panel, its 48 equal configuration outcomes, and its failed grouped model were inspected before this protocol. This follow-up is exploratory and cannot make confirmatory or general elite-base claims.

claims.text: For each of the named seven coordinate-bit bases, the same deterministic PRNG initialization is used within each family and m. Base-specific lift and partial-sum rejection may yield different realized selectors. Compare the resulting PDP top-form intervals by matched family, m and target-kind configuration; do not describe the point tuples as pairwise matched.
A ridge model trained on point-derived and presentation-size features will be evaluated by grouped leave-one-coordinate-bit-base-out validation against the matched-configuration mean baseline.
Exact degree of regularity, FFD, LFD, solving degree, a general elite-base ranking, and ECDLP performance are not inferred from interval-midpoint labels or this seven-base panel.

labeler.execution: top single INPUT_ROOT CERT_DIR followed by top single-replay INPUT_ROOT CERT_DIR

design.planted_sampling: Draw the 27-bit selector uniformly from the frozen deterministic PRNG stream. Decode selector bits into x using the candidate's omitted coordinate bit. Reject non-liftable x and the point that makes a partial sum infinity; continue the same stream until m distinct selected points with non-infinite partial sums are collected. The planted target is their curve sum.
design.natural_target_control: Reuse the saved baseline natural target for the same family and m across all candidate bases; only the sampled factor-base summand tuple changes.
design.common_support_control: Retain the already-generated low-26 common-support panel unchanged as a historical matched-target control; do not pool it with the full-domain panel without a target-distribution feature.
outcomes: top-form quotient interval status and lower/upper bounds
model_features: m, family, target kind, variable count, equation count, binary term count
selected point selector bits and normalized x/y coordinate summaries
design.validation: Group all rows by omitted coordinate-bit base. Seven leave-one-base-out folds; standardize numeric features on training rows only; ridge alpha=10, unpenalized intercept. Predict only finite interval midpoints. Compare absolute error with the mean label for the same family, m, and target kind in training rows. Report folds and aggregate errors; no random row split.
design.decision_rule: Exploratory lead only if aggregate held-out MAE is strictly below matched-configuration baseline MAE and at least five of seven held-out bases improve. Any candidate requires fresh independent target draws and exact regularity/FFD/LFD computation before ranking.
design.persistence: Persist all source manifests, sampled selectors, input JSON and Singular systems, producer/replay logs, top-form certificates, model rows/results, and diagnostics to Git plus s3://setec-astronomy-artifacts. Preserve failures and partial outputs.
design.source_shard_materialization: For each selected point, read the shard locally when present; otherwise locate its exact data/{family}/{file} entry in the candidate s3-file-index.json, fetch the immutable snapshot_key with AWS CLI, and verify bytes and SHA-256 against that index before decoding. Copy the source S3 index into each generated input root. No other shards are downloaded.
design.matching_unit: Matched configuration (curve family, m, target kind) and deterministic PRNG initialization. Candidate-specific lift/rejection can shift subsequent draws; retain and analyze the actual selector list for each base. No paired-point or paired-selector effect is claimed.

required_provenance: factor-base index and family manifest SHA-256
selected base selector for every point
lifted point coordinates and source shard SHA-256
target kind, target coordinates, PRNG seed and rejection policy

analysis_outputs: per-base input counts and selector/point validity checks
per-base top-form producer and replay summaries
grouped-fold rows, predictions, and aggregate lead decision
report with explicit exploratory/post-label and interval-proxy labels
actual selector-list equality/difference table by family, m and base

artifacts.git_metadata: protocol, manifests, source hashes, README and report
artifacts.local_data_retention: Never remove original local or remote run outputs; retries use a new attempt path.

amendment.reason: Clarify the matched-randomization structure before top-form labels are computed. A shared PRNG seed does not guarantee identical realized selector lists because lift and non-infinite-sum rejection depend on each candidate base.
amendment.prior_version_status: V2 froze the generator and was used to generate all 336 inputs. V3 does not change the generator, selected systems, outcome, features, folds, or decision rule. No top-form labels were computed or inspected before this clarification.
amendment.scope_change: None. V3 accurately states that configurations and PRNG initialization are matched, while accepted point selectors may differ by base.
